votes, and do not treat the L1/L2 name itself as a positive or negative label.

visible structure, endpoint, assay, species, formulation, exposure, and
condition. Infer direction from the record cards first, then judge transfer from
all visible context. Do not invent a numeric similarity judgment or assume that
a higher transfer_likelihood must outweigh a concrete experimental mismatch.

Use general medicinal-chemistry knowledge to interpret structures, but ground
every compound-specific empirical claim in the supplied query prior or cited
record cards. Repeated records and multiple cards from one context are not
independent evidence. Return exactly one valid JSON object and do not reveal
hidden chain-of-thought.

claims.claim: The query is a neutral, lipophilic steroid acetal ester (MW 540, logP 4.7, TPSA 99) with a 4-en-3-one and 11-hydroxy; the most structurally relevant steroid/terpenoid contexts all report low oral bioavailability.
AKBA (C15) and withaferin A (C20) show poor oral bioavailability in humans; estradiol (C05, C12, C19, C22) shows 4–11%; β-sitosterol (C01, C14, C21) shows 0.41%; these are affirmative F<20% outcomes.
Complex lipophilic natural products with high MW and poor solubility in the evidence set (paclitaxel, C06/C17/C24) also show low oral F (<8%), consistent with the same direction for the query.

evidence_gaps: No direct oral bioavailability measurement for the query molecule itself is present in the supplied records.
No formulation, dose, or human PK data for the query; oral F can be formulation-dependent.
First-pass metabolism, prodrug activation, and transporter involvement for the query are not directly measured.
Transfer from steroid/terpenoid contexts is structural analogy, not an exact match.
content.decision_summary: Predicted low (F<20%) because the query is a lipophilic, poorly soluble neutral steroid acetal ester, and the most transferable steroid/terpenoid contexts all show measured low oral bioavailability (AKBA poor, withaferin A poor, estradiol 4–11%, β-sitosterol 0.41%, paclitaxel <8%). No affirmative evidence supports F≥20%.
